device.systemGles: GLES: Qualcomm, Adreno (TM) 830, OpenGL ES 3.2 V@0800.64.8

metricDefinitions.pss: Android total process PSS includes proportional sharing. The dumpsys and in-app Debug.MemoryInfo totals can include graphics and swap accounting that is absent from /proc/PID/smaps_rollup Pss. The different sequential readings should not be equated.
metricDefinitions.nativeHeapAppSummary: Android Debug.MemoryInfo summary.native-heap reports private dirty malloc pages. Stock dumpsys Native Heap detail Pss is available separately. Neither measures live allocated bytes.
metricDefinitions.v8: Javet getV8HeapStatistics reports the isolate in bytes. Used, total, physical heap, executable, external memory and malloced memory are distinct, partly overlapping gauges. External memory is not a dedicated ArrayBuffer or GPU counter.
metricDefinitions.comparison: Each row is an independent process launch; soft-GC interventions within one row all use its same live PID, isolate and GL context. Per-stage pair by host and Williams round; pairedMedian is the median of reuse minus before for each pair. For interventions, compute the later-minus-earlier within each run first. Median components do not generally add to the median total.
metricDefinitions.interpretation: Strong references cleared at one point can be investigated by change in V8 used heap after a low-memory notification. Changes across overlapping OS accounting categories, retained heap capacities, graphics-driver pages, allocator reuse, JIT and probe activity cannot be identified as bytes owned by a particular JavaScript object. Android graphics categories are available here; allocator-level per-texture GPU ownership and separate ArrayBuffer resident bytes are unavailable.

priorObservation.limit: Each historical cold process was sampled once after frame 209. Only TOTAL PSS and renderer attribution were saved. The four stock packages had separate package identities. Both baseline profiles occupied only slots one and four; candidates occupied slots two and three. Historical per-category and isolate values are unavailable.

stockApks.method: Reinstalled the four exact #388 stock debug APKs. All runs submitted the original 210 frames. Four Williams blocks put each variant in each slot once. At 4 s after observing the held frame, capture dumpsys meminfo, followed by smaps_rollup and per-mapping smaps. The completion bracket and sequential read windows are recorded per run. Each APK still has a different package identity. Pair baseline and reuse by profile and round; deltas are reuse minus baseline in KiB.
stockApks.accounting: Android App Summary PSS rows form one decomposition of TOTAL PSS. Dalvik detail, mapping categories and smaps_rollup provide overlapping views; do not sum those across sources. GPU mtrack can account for memory outside process smaps. The RSS-only Unknown line in App Summary is excluded. The raw receipt hashes identify the source snapshots; addresses, IDs, package names and mapping paths are omitted.

samePackageDiagnostic.method: Two private debug APKs, one per V8 profile. Within a profile the before and reuse modes share one installation, UID and native libraries but run in different cold processes. The two profile APKs have different application identities. Only the four successive phases inside an individual launch run in the same live process and isolate. Both modes have a diagnostic callback. Reuse installs a counter/clear hook at evaluation. Four Williams rounds, 16 launches, one held terminal frame at 210 submissions.
samePackageDiagnostic.phases: The V8 owner queues a diagnostic task four seconds after submitting frame 209. It samples the live isolate and Android process; repeats after one V8 lowMemoryNotification(), repeats again with the cache retained, then clears only encoder records (before mode uses a no-op) and requests the same V8 low-memory notification once more. Each in-app read obtains V8 statistics before Debug.MemoryInfo and /proc/self/smaps_rollup. Timing within this sequence is approximate. These diagnostic processes did not supply formal performance timings.
samePackageDiagnostic.publicIdentity: Hashes refer to local install receipts and bytes read back from device. For each diagnostic AAR, the listed class files are the only altered payloads compared with its stock AAR. Both APKs allow the same two game bundles; a Java-side hook instruments the source at evaluation. Archive entry names are repository/build artifacts. Device identifiers, install paths and memory addresses are omitted.
interpretation: Each reuse run had 81 privately buffered records, with 5,184 bytes of payload. Heap overhead also includes record metadata, typed arrays and referenced objects. In both profiles the median paired change in used V8 heap after clear plus another low-memory notification, relative to the same no-op sequence, was -23,844 bytes. Standard round 4 went in the opposite direction (+184,464 bytes relative to no-op). It is retained.

The median paired change in total PSS for that clear-versus-no-op step was +18 KiB for standard and 0 KiB for trimmed. At the cleared phase the remaining process difference was +1,213 KiB for standard and +10,073 KiB for trimmed. The latter included an unchanged +8,062 KiB paired median in the Android Graphics summary across the four intervention phases; in the stock Williams comparison that median was -216 KiB. These observations do not assign GPU allocations to the encoder.

Four paired processes per profile cannot uniquely identify the cause of the original multi-megabyte PSS gap. Separate cross-process PSS, same-isolate clear/no-op effects, and V8 used/physical/external statistics before attributing object costs.

incompleteAttempts.reason: ADB preflight timed out before collection. No stage samples were available; the same slot was run successfully.

supplementalAllocatorControl.method: Separate diagnostic APK per V8 profile. In each profile the two encoder modes share one installed package and UID; each run starts a different cold process. Its six stages have the same live PID, isolate and GL context. Two matched pairs per profile; before-starts-first and reuse-starts-first once each. Marker order was predeclared, not randomized across interventions. Relative to stock, an extra diagnostic JNI library only calls Bionic mallopt(M_PURGE_ALL, 0), and the Java host checks for success. The game and renderer libraries remain unchanged. The original bundled JavaScript files are distinct before/reuse variants; diagnostic callbacks are installed at evaluation.
supplementalAllocatorControl.limits: Purge requests release of reclaimable allocator pages, not deallocation of live allocations or universal page release. Debug native allocated/free/size concerns the process allocator; these values are not residency or per-allocation owner measurements. Each phase samples several gauges in sequence. Low-memory notifications and successive snapshots can themselves affect application and kernel accounting. Two pairs give a descriptive contrast, not a population estimate.
interpretation: With all records still held, the first native purge reduced the reuse-minus-before Android Native Heap summary gap by 4,332 KiB in standard V8 and 5,096 KiB in trimmed V8. The corresponding allocated-byte gap stayed within 1.5 KiB of its pre-purge value in both profiles. This demonstrates a material contribution from reclaimable native residency, independent of clearing cached records.

After the following V8 low-memory notification the reuse-minus-before process allocator allocated-byte gap changed from +4,094,776 to -290,856 bytes in standard and from +3,515,880 to +256,952 bytes in trimmed. This associates another difference with a V8 low-memory intervention, without proving which allocator call sites owned the bytes.

Clearing the records after the repeat notification reduced the paired Android Native Heap summary gap by 24 KiB in standard and 2 KiB in trimmed. The final cross-mode process PSS still differed, with a stable Android Graphics summary difference of +4,100 and +3,794 KiB, respectively, throughout this small diagnostic batch. These are Android accounting results, not GPU-object ownership measurements.
